evidence: Theorem 3.6 of arXiv:2607.22686v1 states that a universal vertex forces \(C_s(G)=3\).

For \(K_{1,2,2,2}\), the explicit partition \(\{V\setminus\{a,b,c\},\{a\},\{b\},\{c\}\}\) is valid when \(a,b,c\) lie in the three size-two parts, proving \(C_s=4\) and directly contradicting that theorem.

The published all-set classification implies that any super dominating set in a complete multipartite graph omits at most two vertices, which supplies the upper bound \(C_s\le4\) but not the exact existence criterion for four blocks.
